**The meaning of the verses**
﴿إِذْ يَقُولُ لِصَاحِبِهِ لَا تَحْزَنْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَنَا﴾
… Allah supported him and gave him victory on the day the disbelievers of Quraysh drove him out of his town, Makkah, when he was the second of two (he and Abu Bakr as-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him). They forced the two of them to take shelter in a hollow in Mount Thawr in Makkah, and they stayed there three nights, when he said to his companion Abu Bakr, on seeing his fear for him: "Do not grieve; Allah is with us," with His help and support. So Allah sent down tranquillity into the heart of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and helped him with soldiers whom no human saw, namely the angels, and Allah saved him from his enemy …

﴿وَالَّذِينَ تَبَوَّءُوا الدَّارَ وَالْإِيمَانَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ يُحِبُّونَ مَنْ هَاجَرَ إِلَيْهِمْ وَلَا يَجِدُونَ فِي صُدُورِهِمْ حَاجَةً مِّمَّا أُوتُوا وَيُؤْثِرُونَ عَلَىٰ أَنفُسِهِمْ وَلَوْ كَانَ بِهِمْ خَصَاصَةٌ﴾
And those who settled in Madinah and believed before the Muhajirun emigrated — they are the Ansar — love the Muhajirun and share their wealth with them, and they find in themselves no envy of them for what they were given of the fay' wealth and other things. They put the Muhajirun and those in need before themselves, even if they themselves are in need and poverty. And whoever is saved from stinginess and from holding back surplus wealth, those are the successful, who have attained what they sought.

📖 At-Tafsir Al-Muyassar — King Fahd Complex.

**Talk with your child**
1. When the searchers stood at the mouth of the cave, what did Abu Bakr say? And how did the Prophet ﷺ answer him? And does relying on Allah mean giving up the means? (No; he ﷺ hid in the cave, took a guide and a path other than the usual one, and then relied on Allah.)
2. What did Asma', the daughter of Abu Bakr, do? And why was she called "Dhat an-Nitaqayn"?
3. What did the Ansar do for their brothers the Muhajirun, who had left their homes? And whom can we welcome in the same way?

**This week's exercise**
This week your child welcomes a new classmate, a new neighbour, or a young guest: they show them around and share their toy or their food with them, just as the Ansar shared with the Muhajirun.
